# Model specification: sensor-source 1.0.0

The value source chips read from (hakoniwa,sensor-device with the Hakoniwa Drone aircraft, or the bench source), and the actuator sink the PWM map writes to.

## Features

| Feature | Meaning |
|---|---|
| base | Sample delivery, actuator return, ordering. |

## Terms

| Term | Kind | Feature | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| sample | data | base | Accelerometer, gyroscope, magnetometer, barometer, GNSS values at a model time. |
| sample_period | control | base | Period of the aircraft's sensor samples (from the airframe/link configuration). |
| actuators | data | base | Normalised actuator values from the PWM map. |
| lockstep | control | base | Strict exchange: each sensor sample is answered by an actuator set. |
| tick_order | control | base | Consumers tick before the value source (athrill,tick-before-value-source). |

## Behaviour rules

| Rule | Feature | Rule text |
|---|---|---|
| ADV-SRC-B001 | base | Every chip reading the source at model time t gets the sample whose time is the latest at or before t; all chips see the same sample for the same t. |
| ADV-SRC-B002 | base | At the same clock, chip consumers read the value latched before the source advances (tick_order), so the C-built and Devicetree-built boards see identical values. |
| ADV-SRC-B003 | base | With lockstep, the source advances to the next sample only after the actuator set for the current one is returned; one bootstrap sample starts the exchange; no wall-clock timeout. |
| ADV-SRC-B004 | base | Actuators returned are the PWM map's pulse widths of the last complete period, normalised as the airframe expects. |
| ADV-SRC-B005 | base | GNSS samples are delivered before IMU samples of the same time (HIL_GPS before HIL_SENSOR), so runs are reproducible. |

**Timing.** Samples follow sample_period in model time; the timing rules of docs/device-tree-design.md apply.

**Out of scope.** physics and sensor noise (Hakoniwa Drone), transport details (shared memory, in-process link)
